I made the repair on the year and changed it to 1704. The year's `time.n.08` is position 5 in the gold SBN. I didn't need a WordNet lookup because the concept stays the same and only the year value changes.

**Gold concept positions:**

| Pos | Concept | Pos | Concept |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | queen.n.02 | 8 | time.n.08 |
| 1 | female.n.02 | 9 | person.n.01 |
| 2 | knight.v.01 | 10 | scientist.n.01 |
| 3 | time.n.08 | 11 | time.n.08 |
| 4 | male.n.02 ("Newton") | 12 | knight.v.01 |
| 5 | time.n.08 (year 1705) | 13 | male.n.02 |
| 6 | male.n.02 ("He") | 14 | work.n.02 |
| 7 | be.v.02 | | |

**Building the repair:**
- **Inverting the year link (②):** `knight.v.01 Time +3` points from before the `CORRECTION` box to the year, so I removed it from the verb. Both year concepts now carry `TimeOf` back to the verb: `TimeOf -3` on the 1704 reparandum and `TimeOf -4` on the 1705 repair. That gives the reparandum its required edge (R5).
- **Box pointer (R6):** `CONTINUATION <1` becomes `CONTINUATION <3`, because it has to count back over the two new boxes.
- **Index shifts (R1):** the "He" in the second sentence now sits at position 7. Its `ANA -2` becomes `ANA -3`, so it still lands on Newton (position 4).
- **One restructured link:** the `male.n.02 ANA -9` on "his" would need to become `ANA -10` to reach Newton. That is outside the ±9 limit and the SBN reader would misread it. Following the manual's advice to restructure in that case, it now points to "He" instead (`ANA -7`). "He" already refers back to Newton, so the meaning is the same. This is the only change beyond what the repair itself requires.

I recounted every other index in the second sentence, and each still lands on the same concept as in the gold SBN.
